updates.note: Year-end depot feature: said workers came back to tarped, wet hangars and went to work; holiday message 'Rest. Hug your kids... We'll see you in January'; said many employees are spending leave hanging drywall at home.
Holiday message to base families: sailors, civilians and families carried a heavy load; station operating, squadrons flying, take a real break.

Day-95 beat (still waiting on repairs): hallway ceiling leaks into a bucket her kids named 'Bob'; back bedroom smells of mildew; landlord says repairs 'after the holidays'; aid application started in November is stuck at 'pending'; said she'll make coffee if a door-to-door team ever knocks. New detail: the bucket 'Bob'.
Said Rosa is 'not a case number'; door to door must mean every door and returning when nobody answers.
On the Navy security review: would not discuss specific security measures; said the station is operating and a review is what you do after a season like this one.
On the security review: channel safety comes first; teams finished a full sweep before the channel reopened; a review asks what was learned.
To the national wire: the Navy takes each incident seriously and owes it to people near installations to look hard at what happened.

Welcomed the Navy review; repeated he never claimed to know what the lights were, only that they weren't stars or planes; has filmed nothing unusual over the base since; still photographs Jupiter and Saturn; advice: note time and direction, call it in, then post.
Status piece on the county audit, Navy suspension and federal IG review of the debris and fuel contracts; notes records requests pending.
Restated denial of overbilling: 'working around the clock since the week of the storm, and we stand behind every load.'
Said all product Quellmar delivered met specifications and she expects the Navy review to show it.
Year-end comment on the AIS anomaly: 'consistent with spoofing'; who was transmitting is still open and public data alone won't answer it.
Said the wastewater signal appeared while ER visits were still climbing and gave early warning; slower recovery in low-income neighborhoods is 'rarely one thing'; holiday hand-washing advice.

Look-back on the boil-water weeks: knew it was bad when stretchers lined the hallway before lunch; refused to discuss patients; praised nurses who boiled water at home and still worked twelve-hour shifts.
On the equity findings: 'Numbers like that don't sit on a shelf'; door-to-door registration is one step.

Said the 911 data shows the size of the gap, not the reason, and calls must be traced; recommends tracking response times by neighborhood in real time and starting outreach where there are fewest cars and phones; analysis compared census tracts.

Keeps a printout of MV Gulf Provider's last position on his office wall; lesson: cargo was ready but the channel wasn't; wants a plan B pre-positioned inland and by truck and clearer priority for relief cargo after reopenings.

New detail: reopened his gutted shop in December with new drywall, half-stocked shelves and new Christmas lights; cash register survived the flood; regulars stop by mostly to check on him; open through Christmas Eve, closed Christmas Day; recalled the blast ('the pelicans didn't either').
Came to the hub with her three kids on Christmas Eve, left with tamales and oranges; roof still leaking.

Ran Christmas Eve at the fellowship hall (tamales in borrowed roasters, donated coats, toys); keeps a penciled binder of neighbors' needs; 'I've got a list of doors'; hub stays open after the holidays.
Told families the station is open and training continues; families will hear from public affairs first if they need to do anything differently.
Said monitoring doesn't mean walking away; testing before any reopening; 'We'll open when the data says so, not before.'
Explained the surge as a bulldozer pushing oil into marshes a normal tide never reaches; marsh recovery uncertain, spring growth will tell more.
Urged every vessel operator to read the joint advisory and review vendor remote access; will not discuss the open investigation.
Day-105 beat (advisory release): remote maintenance is a door into the ship; review vendor access, separate cargo control, patch, review again.
Said Rendal is cooperating fully and will review the advisory with customers; vessel-system questions are for operators and investigators.
Supports the advisory; said Brightwake shut off every remote session in September and has been rebuilding how access works; 'We were the ones whose credentials were misused.'
'The fix isn't exotic': know which vendors have access, turn it off when unneeded, read the logs.
Explained vendor remote access as 'a spare key you gave the plumber'; declined to guess who was behind the misuse before investigators say.
Year-in-review quote: 'this one didn't end when the wind stopped'; will remember neighbors who showed up before officials could.
Year-end: proud of sailors, civilians and families who kept the station running.
Year-end image: workers bailing water from hangars in the morning and turning wrenches by afternoon.
New-year advice: residents without cars should register for evacuation assistance well before June; write neighbors' numbers on paper because phones die.
Announced plan to harden O.N. Stevens power feeds: 'when the power goes, the pumps go'; apologized that it took a storm.
Welcomed state bridge wind-closure review: closures cut the county in half.
Reacted to the hardening plan: kept a spreadsheet of who needed jugs and who could drive during the notice; wants a schedule and a contact.

On the bridge review: 'Two ways off this beach, and they both close'; wants the plan announced ahead of time. New details: he welded steel along the ship channel for a living; now keeps a week of supplies and a full tank.
Said hardening the feeds comes first; utility will share details as the plan develops.
Said the right parts were 'in the wrong building, under water'; Delta is looking at keeping critical stock farther inland; still sorry about the delay.
Said the attribution doesn't change the work: test, monitor, reopen when safe.
Heard the attribution while mending a net in Aransas Pass: 'Somebody did this... My nets are still dry'; claim still pending; 'Tell me when I can fish.'
Said Rendal has cooperated fully since day one; the announcement is the government's to explain.
Said the channel is open and port conditions unchanged by the attribution; Coast Guard won't comment on its details; operators should complete the December advisory review.
Joked about islanders' theories of the blast; customers asking about the attribution all afternoon.
Mentioned only, as the injured deckhand who said in December he was recovering.
Reacted to attribution: 'I'd like a name'; blast came off the port bow; prefers to talk about his crew; crew always watched the water at the jetties, 'Now we know why.'
Said attribution gives the blast a category and changes how buyers and insurers think about the next storm, not barrels today.
Wrote an opinion column urging a local plan that treats the next hurricane as a security event.
Day-114 beat: reported the civil forfeiture filing naming Brannoch Maritime Holdings (director L. Marrick) as shared owner and about $3.9M in diverted aid.
Day-114 beat: 'The filing speaks for itself'; owners can respond in court; would not elaborate on how aid was diverted.
Said Vantorra 'did the work we were hired to do' and will respond through attorneys; did not answer questions about ownership (never names Brannoch).
Statement: all product met specifications; Quellmar will respond in court.
After the filing: applicants whose deposit info was changed will be made whole; never give a password to anyone who calls, texts or knocks.
Reacted to the $3.9M figure: families on her list got 'nothing, or half of nothing'; 'The roof on the next block can't wait for a judge.'
Cautioned against blending the equity gap with diverted aid; will keep tracking aid by tract once door-to-door registration is under way.
Announced partial reopening: reopened what testing supports; urged people to file claims and keep receipts and trip logs.
Partial reopening is 'part of a living'; filed his claim in November; still paying on the boat; wants to look at the water before trusting it; 'Four thousand two hundred people waiting. I'm one.'
On the forfeiture filing: aware of it, will let it speak for itself; base services not affected; declined to discuss the fuel review's status.
Wrote an opinion column urging the county and FEMA to finish door-to-door registration and publish progress by neighborhood.
Start-of-2028 comment: channel open, customers shipping; hurricane readiness 'isn't the whole job anymore'; declined security specifics; 'We'd like a boring summer.'

Look-back: landlord patched the hallway leak the first week of January ('Bob is retired'); aid application still pending; still awaiting door-to-door registration; done when her kids stop asking if the water is coming back.
Look-back: 'Some water open. No check yet. Boat payment every month.'
Look-back: shop stocked again, mostly ('Two-thirds of a store and all of the jokes'); counting weeks to spring break.
Look-back: kept her water-run spreadsheet, deleted the jug column, kept the phone numbers; wants dates for the plant hardening: 'A plan without a deadline is a wish.'
Look-back: grateful to those who got him out; wants to know how they will protect the next crew. New detail: arm out of the cast and cleared to return to work ('It's what I do').
Look-back: sorting donated blankets at the hall; wants reviewers to spend a morning answering her door before writing the report; 'Ask me again at a year.'
